claim: Complete ablation of DMP1-positive osteocytes in Dmp1cre Rosa26em1Cin(SA-IRES-Loxp-ZsGreen-stop-Loxp-DTA) homozygotes (DTAho) caused lethality of mice before birth.
source: The results showed that complete ablation of DMP1-positive osteocytes (osteocyteDMP1) in Dmp1cre Rosa26em1Cin(SA-IRES-Loxp-ZsGreen-stop-Loxp-DTA) homozygotes (DTAho) caused lethality of mice before birth.
evidence: Direct observation from the experimental mouse model described in the manuscript.

claim: DTAhet mice had more empty lacunae without the presence of osteocytes within cortical and trabecular bone matrix compared to WT mice.
source: As shown in Figure 1A and B, DTAhet mice had more empty lacunae without the presence of osteocytes within cortical and trabecular bone matrix compared to WT mice.
evidence: Histological analysis shown in Figure 1A and B demonstrates increased empty lacunae in DTAhet mice.

claim: Reduced dendrites were observed in residual osteocytes of DTAhet mice.
source: Further, reduced dendrites were also observed in residual osteocytes of DTAhet mice (Figure 1C and D), indicating the impairment of osteocyte network.
evidence: Immunofluorescence staining and quantification shown in Figure 1C and D.

claim: About 80% empty lacunae was observed in DTAhet mice at 13 weeks, which increased by about 20% compared to 4 weeks.
source: About 80% empty lacunae was observed in DTAhet mice at 13 weeks, which increased by about 20% compared to 4 weeks (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C), indicating that diphtheria toxin (DT) had an accumulative effect with age in DTAhet mice.
evidence: Quantification data from histological analysis at two time points.

claim: Alizarin red/Alcian blue staining of whole-mount skeleton at E19.0 showed no apparent differences of craniofacial, long bones or spines between WT and DTAhet mice.
source: Interestingly, Alizarin red/Alcian blue staining of whole-mount skeleton at E19.0 showed no apparent differences of craniofacial, long bones or spines between WT and DTAhet mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Whole-mount skeletal staining shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: DTAhet mice exhibited significant decrease in femur bone mineral density (BMD), bone volume fraction (BV/TV), trabecular number (Tb.N), trabecular thickness (Tb.Th), as well as greater trabecular separation (Tb.Sp) compared to WT mice at 4 weeks.
source: Micro-computed tomography (μCT) examination of the appendicular skeleton revealed a significant decrease in femur bone mineral density (BMD), bone volume fraction (BV/TV), trabecular number (Tb.N), trabecular thickness (Tb.Th), as well as greater trabecular separation (Tb.Sp) in DTAhet mice compared to those in WT mice at 4 weeks (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: μCT analysis data shown in Figure 2A and B.

claim: Ablation of osteocytes led to cortical bone loss with decreased cortical thickness (Ct.Th) and increased cortical porosity (Ct.Po).
source: Moreover, ablation of osteocytes also led to cortical bone loss with decreased cortical thickness (Ct.Th) and increased cortical porosity (Ct.Po) (Figure 2A and C).
evidence: μCT analysis data shown in Figure 2A and C.

claim: At 13 weeks, DTAhet mice exhibited more bone loss in both trabecular and cortical bone compared to WT mice.
source: At 13 weeks, DTAhet mice exhibited more bone loss in both trabecular and cortical bone compared to those in WT mice (Figure 2D–G).
evidence: μCT analysis data shown in Figure 2D–G.

claim: The phenotype observed is unique and gender-insensitive.
source: The phenotype observed is unique and gender-insensitive (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: Analysis of female mice shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–C.

claim: There was no increase of bone mass of vertebral bodies from 4 to 13 weeks in DTAhet mice.
source: Furthermore, there was no increase of bone mass of vertebral bodies from 4 to 13 weeks in DTAhet mice (Figure 2J and K), suggesting the retardation of vertebral body maturation.
evidence: μCT analysis data comparing two time points shown in Figure 2J and K.

claim: At 13 weeks, obvious kyphosis occurred in DTAhet mice due to severe osteoporosis and vertebral body compression.
source: At 13 weeks, obvious kyphosis occurred in DTAhet mice (Figure 2L) due to serve osteoporosis and vertebral body compression.
evidence: Gross images and whole-body μCT shown in Figure 2L.

claim: At the age of 30 weeks, almost all of DTAhet mice developed severe kyphosis.
source: At the age of 30 weeks, almost all of DTAhet mice developed severe kyphosis (Figure 2N).
evidence: Whole-body μCT images shown in Figure 2N.

claim: DTAhet mice at 4 weeks had abnormal steps when running.
source: Consistent with the development of kyphosis, gait analysis revealed that DTAhet mice at 4 weeks had abnormal steps when running (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: Gait analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: The front and hind stride length were much shorter in DTAhet mice.
source: The front and hind stride length were much shorter in DTAhet mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: Gait analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The swing speed of DTAhet mice was much slower than WT mice.
source: Also, the swing speed of DTAhet mice was much slower than WT mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D, Videos 1–6).
evidence: Gait analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2D and Videos 1–6.

claim: There was a continual body weight loss and muscle weight loss in DTAhet mice from 4 weeks.
source: Whole-body examination of DTAhet mice revealed there was a continual body weight loss and muscle weight loss (Figure 3A–C) from 4 weeks.
evidence: Body weight and muscle weight measurements shown in Figure 3A–C.

claim: Histology examination of gastrocnemius muscles revealed focal muscle atrophy with mild inflammation at 4 weeks.
source: Histology examination of gastrocnemius muscles revealed focal muscle atrophy with mild inflammation at 4 weeks (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: Histological analysis shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: Many myonuclei were mispositioned and became centralized in DTAhet mice in contrast to those in WT mice.
source: Many myonuclei were mispositioned and became centralized in contrast to those in WT mice.
evidence: Histological observation of muscle tissue.

claim: At 13 weeks, there was continual muscle atrophy, rimmed vacuoles, and inclusion bodies seen within the muscle fibers.
source: At 13 weeks, there was continual muscle atrophy, rimmed vacuoles, and inclusion bodies seen within the muscle fibers (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: Histological analysis shown in Figure 3F and G.

claim: There was no reduction of numbers of muscle fibers after osteocyte ablation at 4 weeks and 13 weeks in DTAhet mice compared to WT mice.
source: To preclude the direct target of DMP1 on muscle, we quantified the number of muscle fibers and the results showed that there was no reduction of numbers of muscle fibers after osteocyte ablation at 4 weeks (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A) and 13 weeks in DTAhet mice compared to WT mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Quantification of muscle fiber numbers shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: The level of Dmp1 expression in muscle was very weak and far less than bone.
source: Measurement of Dmp1 expression in WT muscle showed that the level of Dmp1 expression in muscle was very weak and far less than bone (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: RT-qPCR analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The average lifespan of DTAhet mice was about 20–40 weeks, which was much shorter than WT mice.
source: Analysis of lifespan in these mice further revealed the average lifespan of DTAhet mice was about 20–40 weeks, which was much shorter than WT mice (Figure 3H).
evidence: Kaplan–Meier survival curve shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Downregulated genes by osteocyte ablation were enriched in ossification, osteoblast differentiation, positive regulation of osteoblast differentiation, endochondral ossification, and bone morphogenesis.
source: Selected skeleton-related Gene Ontology (GO) analysis revealed that downregulated genes by osteocyte ablation were enriched in ossification, osteoblast differentiation, positive regulation of osteoblast differentiation, endochondral ossification, and bone morphogenesis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: GO analysis of RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Genes that are critical for osteogenesis, including Alpl, Bglap, Col1a1, Spp1, Sp7, and Runx2, were affected by the ablation of osteocytes.
source: Heatmap of significantly differentiated genes (fold change >2.0-fold, WT average FPKM > 10, false discovery rate [FDR] < 0.05) and subsequent RT-qPCR verified that genes that are critical for osteogenesis, including Alpl, Bglap, Col1a1, Spp1, Sp7, and Runx2, were affected by the ablation of osteocytes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: RNA sequencing heatmap and RT-qPCR verification shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: Osteogenesis-related pathways, including Wnt signaling pathway, Hedgehog signaling pathway, and Notch signaling pathway, were downregulated.
source: Also, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed that osteogenesis-related pathways, including Wnt signaling pathway, Hedgehog signaling pathway, and Notch signaling pathway, were downregulated (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–F).
evidence: GSEA analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D–F.

claim: The number of osteoblasts (N.Ob/BS) and osteoid-covered surface (OS/BS) was remarkably reduced in DTAhet mice compared to WT mice.
source: In addition, the number of osteoblasts (N.Ob/BS) and osteoid-covered surface (OS/BS) was remarkably reduced in DTAhet mice compared to WT mice (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: Histomorphometry analysis shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: Bone marrow fat accumulation in DTAhet mice was observed.
source: Also, bone marrow fat accumulation in DTAhet mice was observed (Figure 4C and D).
evidence: Histological analysis shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: Mineral surface (MS/BS), mineral apposition rate (MAR), and bone formation rate (BFR/BS) were significantly decreased in DTAhet mice.
source: The result showed that mineral surface (MS/BS), mineral apposition rate (MAR), and bone formation rate (BFR/BS) were significantly decreased in DTAhet mice (Figure 4E and F).
evidence: Dynamic histomorphometric analysis using calcein labeling shown in Figure 4E and F.

claim: Serum procollagen type 1 N-terminal propeptide (P1NP), a bone formation index, was reduced after osteocyte ablation.
source: Serum procollagen type 1 N-terminal propeptide (P1NP), a bone formation index, was also reduced after osteocyte ablation (Figure 4G).
evidence: ELISA measurement shown in Figure 4G.

claim: There were decreased osteogenesis and mineralization in DTAhet mice compared to WT mice at both time points of 4 and 13 weeks.
source: Intriguingly, in vitro osteogenesis showed that there were also decreased osteogenesis and mineralization in DTAhet mice compared to WT mice at both time points of 4 and 13 weeks and the impairment of osteogenesis was greater in DTAhet mice at 13 weeks compared to 4 weeks (Figure 4H and I).
evidence: In vitro osteogenesis assay shown in Figure 4H and I.

claim: The mRNA level of osteogenic markers at 4 weeks, including Alpl, Bglap, and Runx2, was decreased.
source: And the mRNA level of osteogenic markers at 4 weeks, including Alpl, Bglap, and Runx2, was also decreased (Figure 4J).
evidence: RT-qPCR analysis shown in Figure 4J.

claim: Osteoclast surface (Oc.S/BS) and numbers (N.Oc/BS) were significantly increased after osteocytes deletion.
source: In the aspect of osteoclastogenesis, histomorphometry analysis revealed that osteoclast surface (Oc.S/BS) and numbers (N.Oc/BS) were significantly increased after osteocytes deletion (Figure 4K and L).
evidence: Histomorphometry analysis shown in Figure 4K and L.

claim: Circulatory RANKL was increased in DTAhet mice.
source: Circulatory RANKL was also increased in DTAhet mice (Figure 4M).
evidence: ELISA measurement shown in Figure 4M.

claim: Circulatory osteoprotegrin (OPG), a decoy receptor of RANKL, was decreased.
source: In contrast, circulatory osteoprotegrin (OPG), a decoy receptor of RANKL, was decreased (Figure 4M), leading to the elevated ratio of RANKL/OPG (Figure 4M).
evidence: ELISA measurement shown in Figure 4M.

claim: Serum collagen type I c-telopeptide (CTX), a bone resorption index, was significantly augmented in DTAhet mice compared to WT mice.
source: Serum collagen type I c-telopeptide (CTX), a bone resorption index, was also significantly augmented in DTAhet mice compared to WT mice (Figure 4N), which implicated a high level of osteoclast activity of DTAhet mice in vivo.
evidence: ELISA measurement shown in Figure 4N.

claim: There was a slight increase (less than 1%) of osteoclast progenitors (B220-CD11bloLy-6Chi) in DTAhet mice at 4 weeks compared to WT mice.
source: Also, flow cytometry analysis revealed that there was a slight increase (less than 1%) of osteoclast progenitors (B220-CD11bloLy-6Chi) in DTAhet mice at 4 weeks compared to WT mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1G and H).
evidence: Flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1G and H.

claim: Osteoclastogenesis was increased in DTAhet mice compared to WT mice at both time points of 4 and 13 weeks.
source: The results showed that osteoclastogenesis was increased in DTAhet mice compared to WT mice at both time points (Figure 4O and Q).
evidence: In vitro osteoclastogenesis assay shown in Figure 4O and Q.

claim: The induction of osteoclastogenesis was greater in DTAhet mice at 13 weeks compared to 4 weeks.
source: Interestingly, the induction of osteoclastogenesis was greater in DTAhet mice at 13 weeks compared to 4 weeks (Figure 4P and Q), suggesting the time-dependent accumulative effect of osteoclastogenesis in DTAhet mice.
evidence: In vitro osteoclastogenesis assay shown in Figure 4P and Q.

claim: The expression of the signature genes of osteoclasts, including Acp5, Calcr, and Ocstamp, at the mRNA level was significantly upregulated in DTAhet mice.
source: Also, the expression of the signature genes of osteoclasts, including Acp5, Calcr, and Ocstamp, at the mRNA level was significantly upregulated in DTAhet mice (Figure 4Q).
evidence: RT-qPCR analysis shown in Figure 4Q (note: the text refers to Figure 4Q but likely means Figure 4R based on the figure layout).

claim: Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed 10 distinct populations including B cell, hematopoietic stem cell and progenitor cell (HSPC), megakaryocyte, neutrophil, erythrocyte, monocyte, dendritic cell (DC), macrophage, T cell, and MSC.
source: After rigorous quality control, gene expression data from 26,562 cells (13,835 and 12,727 cells from 4-week littermate WT and DTAhet mice, respectively) were compiled for clustering analysis and revealed 10 distinct populations visualized with Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) embeddings (Figure 5A–C). These 10 distinct populations included B cell, hematopoietic stem cell and progenitor cell (HSPC), megakaryocyte, neutrophil, erythrocyte, monocyte, dendritic cell (DC), macrophage, T cell, and MSC (Figure 5A and C).
evidence: Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis shown in Figure 5A–C.

claim: Proportion analysis revealed a significant expansion of neutrophils in DTAhet mice.
source: Proportion analysis revealed a significant expansion of neutrophils in DTAhet mice (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: Single-cell RNA sequencing proportion analysis shown in Figure 5D and E.

claim: The number of B cells was significantly less in DTAhet mice than that in WT mice.
source: Also, the number of B cells was significantly less in DTAhet mice than that in WT mice (Figure 5D and E), which implicated that osteocytes ablation induced lymphoid–myeloid malfunction in the bone marrow.
evidence: Single-cell RNA sequencing proportion analysis shown in Figure 5D and E.

claim: DTAhet mice had stronger directionality of velocity vectors from the HSPC population to the neutrophil population compared to WT mice.
source: The result showed that DTAhet mice had stronger directionality of velocity vectors from the HSPC population to the neutrophil population compared to WT mice (Figure 5F), implying that osteocytes deletion altered HSPC differentiation.
evidence: RNA velocity analysis shown in Figure 5F.

claim: There was a significantly higher pseudotime density distribution in G4 cell (a subcluster of neutrophil) in DTAhet mice.
source: Meanwhile, myeloid trajectory analysis revealed that there was a significantly higher pseudotime density distribution in G4 cell (a subcluster of neutrophil) in DTAhet mice (Figure 5G).
evidence: Myeloid trajectory analysis shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Lymphoid trajectory analysis demonstrated a relatively lower pseudotime density distribution in pre-B cell and immature B cell (subclusters of B cell) in DTAhet mice.
source: In contrast, lymphoid trajectory analysis demonstrated a relatively lower pseudotime density distribution in pre-B cell and immature B cell (subclusters of B cell) in DTAhet mice (Figure 5H).
evidence: Lymphoid trajectory analysis shown in Figure 5H.

claim: DTAhet mice demonstrated significantly increased number of short-term HSCs (ST-HSCs) with decreased number of long-term HSCs (LT-HSCs).
source: Although there was no significant change in HSC (Lin-c-Kit+Sca1+, LSK+ cell) numbers between DTAhet and WT mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and B), DTAhet mice demonstrated significantly increased number of short-term HSCs (ST-HSCs) with decreased number of long-term HSCs (LT-HSCs), indicating that HSCs in DTAhet mice bone marrow were mobilized (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C and D).
evidence: Flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2C and D.

claim: The number of myeloid progenitors, including common myeloid progenitors (CMP), granulocyte–monocyte progenitors (GMP), and common monocyte progenitors (cMoP), was substantially increased after osteocyte ablation.
source: Further flow cytometry analysis revealed that the number of myeloid progenitors, including common myeloid progenitors (CMP), granulocyte–monocyte progenitors (GMP), and common monocyte progenitors (cMoP), was substantially increased after osteocyte ablation (Figure 5I and J, Figure 5—figure supplement 2E and F), and megakaryocyte erythroid progenitors (MEP) numbers were decreased (Figure 5I and J).
evidence: Flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 5I and J, Figure 5—figure supplement 2E and F.

claim: Total CD11b+ myeloid cells were increased in DTAhet mice.
source: Meanwhile, total CD11b+ myeloid cells were also increased (Figure 5K and L) in DTAhet mice, in which both neutrophils and monocytes significantly expanded (Figure 5M and N, Figure 5—figure supplement 2G and H).
evidence: Flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 5K and L.

claim: Both neutrophils and monocytes significantly expanded in DTAhet mice.
source: Meanwhile, total CD11b+ myeloid cells were also increased (Figure 5K and L) in DTAhet mice, in which both neutrophils and monocytes significantly expanded (Figure 5M and N, Figure 5—figure supplement 2G and H).
evidence: Flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 5M and N, Figure 5—figure supplement 2G and H.

claim: The proportion of common lymphoid progenitors (CLP) was not altered in DTAhet mice.
source: In addition, while the proportion of common lymphoid progenitors (CLP) was not altered in DTAhet mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 2I and J), total B220+ lymphoid cells reduced remarkably after osteocyte ablation (Figure 5O and P), in which DTAhet mice showed a relatively lower proportion of early B cell (pro-B pre-B, immature B, and transitional B cell) and a relatively higher proportion of late B cell (early mature B and late mature B) (Figure 5Q and R), which suggested that B cell development was impaired along the immature B to mature B cell transition in DTAhet mice.
evidence: Flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2I and J.

claim: Total B220+ lymphoid cells reduced remarkably after osteocyte ablation.
source: In addition, while the proportion of common lymphoid progenitors (CLP) was not altered in DTAhet mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 2I and J), total B220+ lymphoid cells reduced remarkably after osteocyte ablation (Figure 5O and P), in which DTAhet mice showed a relatively lower proportion of early B cell (pro-B pre-B, immature B, and transitional B cell) and a relatively higher proportion of late B cell (early mature B and late mature B) (Figure 5Q and R), which suggested that B cell development was impaired along the immature B to mature B cell transition in DTAhet mice.
evidence: Flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 5O and P.

claim: DTAhet mice showed a relatively lower proportion of early B cell (pro-B pre-B, immature B, and transitional B cell) and a relatively higher proportion of late B cell (early mature B and late mature B).
source: In addition, while the proportion of common lymphoid progenitors (CLP) was not altered in DTAhet mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 2I and J), total B220+ lymphoid cells reduced remarkably after osteocyte ablation (Figure 5O and P), in which DTAhet mice showed a relatively lower proportion of early B cell (pro-B pre-B, immature B, and transitional B cell) and a relatively higher proportion of late B cell (early mature B and late mature B) (Figure 5Q and R), which suggested that B cell development was impaired along the immature B to mature B cell transition in DTAhet mice.
evidence: Flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 5Q and R.

claim: G4 population was significantly increased in DTAhet mice compared to WT mice.
source: As scRNA-seq revealed that neutrophils underwent a significant change after osteocyte ablation, neutrophil population were further reclustered into four subclusters from G1 to G4 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A and B) and G4 population was significantly increased in DTAhet mice compared to WT mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 3C and D), which implied that osteocyte ablation accelerated neutrophil maturation.
evidence: Single-cell RNA sequencing reclustering analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3C and D.

claim: Neutrophil functions, including activation and chemotaxis, were all upregulated in DTAhet mice.
source: Consistent with this observation, neutrophil functions, including activation and chemotaxis, were all upregulated in DTAhet mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 3E and F).
evidence: Functional score analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3E and F.

claim: Genes related to glycolysis and necroptosis were upregulated in neutrophils of DTAhet mice.
source: Genes related to glycolysis and necroptosis were also upregulated (Figure 5—figure supplement 3G and H), indicating that osteocyte ablation altered neutrophil functions.
evidence: Functional score analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3G and H.

claim: Total bone marrow had increased senescence with a higher SASP score in DTAhet mice compared to WT mice.
source: ScRNA-seq revealed that total bone marrow had increased senescence with a higher SASP score in DTAhet mice compared to WT mice (Figure 6A).
evidence: Single-cell RNA sequencing SASP score analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: DTAhet mice had increased maturity in bone marrow reflected from RNA velocity.
source: DTAhet mice also had increased maturity in bone marrow reflected from RNA velocity (Figure 6B).
evidence: RNA velocity latent time analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Circulatory SASP index, including TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, were elevated in DTAhet mice.
source: Meanwhile, circulatory SASP index, including TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, were also elevated in DTAhet mice (Figure 6C).
evidence: ELISA measurements shown in Figure 6C.

claim: MSC, CMP, monocyte, and its subcluster Ly6c2_monocyte, neutrophil, and its subcluster G2, G3, and G4, had increased SASP scores.
source: Further scRNA-seq analysis uncovered that MSC, CMP, monocyte, and its subcluster Ly6c2_monocyte, neutrophil, and its subcluster G2, G3, and G4, had increased SASP scores (Figure 6D–G) and higher-level expressions of senescence-related genes in DTAhet mice (Figure 6H).
evidence: Single-cell RNA sequencing SASP score analysis shown in Figure 6D–G.

claim: RT-qPCR verified the elevated senescence with increased gene expressions, including Cdkn2a and Cdkn1a in DTAhet mice.
source: RT-qPCR also verified the elevated senescence with increased gene expressions, including Cdkn2a and Cdkn1a in DTAhet mice (Figure 6I and J).
evidence: RT-qPCR analysis shown in Figure 6I and J.

claim: There were obvious increased numbers of SA-βGal+ cell in the primary spongiosa, bone marrow, and cortical bone in DTAhet mice compared to WT mice.
source: Further, senescence-associated β-galactosidase (SA-βGal) staining revealed that there were obvious increased numbers of SA-βGal+ cell in the primary spongiosa, bone marrow, and cortical bone in DTAhet mice compared to WT mice (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: SA-βGal staining shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Downregulated genes after osteocyte ablation were enriched in ossification and biomineral tissue development.
source: GO analysis revealed that downregulated genes after osteocyte ablation were enriched in ossification and biomineral tissue development (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), which was consistent with the finding of impaired osteoblast differentiation (Figure 4H–J).
evidence: GO analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The mRNA level of adipogenic markers, including Adipoq, Fabp4, Pparg, and Cebpa, was significantly increased.
source: Meanwhile, the mRNA level of adipogenic markers, including Adipoq, Fabp4, Pparg, and Cebpa, was significantly increased (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C), indicating increased adipogenesis and alteration of MSC commitment after osteocyte ablation.
evidence: RT-qPCR analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The mRNA levels of cartilage anabolism-related genes (Col1a2, Acan, Sox9, and Prg4) and catabolism-related genes (Mmp3, Mmp13, Adamts1, and Adamts5) were not significantly changed.
source: In addition, the mRNA levels of cartilage anabolism-related genes (Col1a2, Acan, Sox9, and Prg4) and catabolism-related genes (Mmp3, Mmp13, Adamts1, and Adamts5) were not significantly changed (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D), indicating that chondrogenesis was not altered after osteocyte ablation.
evidence: RT-qPCR analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The subclusters 2 and 4 of Ly6c2+ monocytes demonstrated the enrichment of osteoclast differentiation-related genes after osteocyte ablation.
source: Similarly, Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) analysis revealed that the subclusters 2 and 4 of Ly6c2+ monocytes demonstrated the enrichment of osteoclast differentiation-related genes after osteocyte ablation (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E and F), which was corroborated in our enhanced in vitro osteoclast differentiation (Figure 4O–R).
evidence: KEGG analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E and F.

claim: Osteocytes play critical roles in regulation of lineage cell specifications in bone and bone marrow through mediation of senescence.
source: Together, we showed that osteocytes play critical roles in regulation of lineage cell specifications in bone and bone marrow through mediation of senescence.
evidence: Summary statement based on the collective findings of the study.

claim: Partial ablation of DMP1-positive osteocytes caused severe sarcopenia, osteoporosis, and degenerative kyphosis, leading to shorter lifespan in these animals.
source: Using a mouse model of conditional deletion of osteocytes by the expression of diphtheria toxin subunit α in dentin matrix protein 1 (DMP1)-positive osteocytes, we demonstrated that partial ablation of DMP1-positive osteocytes caused severe sarcopenia, osteoporosis, and degenerative kyphosis, leading to shorter lifespan in these animals.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings from the mouse model.

claim: Osteocytes reduction altered mesenchymal lineage commitment, resulting in impairment of osteogenesis and induction of osteoclastogensis.
source: Osteocytes reduction altered mesenchymal lineage commitment, resulting in impairment of osteogenesis and induction of osteoclastogensis.
evidence: Summary of findings on mesenchymal lineage changes.

claim: Hematopoietic lineage was mobilized toward myeloid lineage differentiation with expanded myeloid progenitors, neutrophils, and monocytes, while the lymphopoiesis was impaired with reduced B cells in the osteocyte ablation mice.
source: Single-cell RNA sequencing further revealed that hematopoietic lineage was mobilized toward myeloid lineage differentiation with expanded myeloid progenitors, neutrophils, and monocytes, while the lymphopoiesis was impaired with reduced B cells in the osteocyte ablation mice.
evidence: Summary of single-cell RNA sequencing findings on hematopoietic lineage changes.

claim: The acquisition of a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) in both osteogenic and myeloid lineage cells was the underlying cause.
source: The acquisition of a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) in both osteogenic and myeloid lineage cells was the underlying cause.
evidence: Summary statement identifying SASP as the mechanistic cause.

claim: Osteocytes, as the long-living terminally differentiated cells and the most abundant cells within the bone matrix, play vital roles in maintaining the skeletal homeostasis.
source: Osteocytes, as the long-living terminally differentiated cells and the most abundant cells within the bone matrix (Tresguerres et al., 2020), play vital roles in maintaining the skeletal homeostasis.
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Tresguerres et al., 2020.

claim: Osteocytes have been shown to regulate bone formation, bone resorption, bone marrow hematopoiesis.
source: Apart from mechanical transduction (Long, 2011; Sato et al., 2020), osteocytes have been shown to regulate bone formation, bone resorption, bone marrow hematopoiesis (Asada et al., 2013; Azab et al., 2020; Fulzele et al., 2013; Xiao et al., 2021), and generate endocrine signals to mediate function of other organs (Razzaque, 2009; Fulzele et al., 2017; Cain et al., 2012).
evidence: Statement supported by multiple citations.

claim: Sclerostin, one of the key inhibitors of Wnt signaling pathway, is mainly produced by osteocytes.
source: Sclerostin, one of the key inhibitors of Wnt signaling pathway, is mainly produced by osteocytes (Tresguerres et al., 2020).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Tresguerres et al., 2020.

claim: NO and PGE2 secretion by osteocytes in response to mechanical stimulation have anabolic effects on osteoblasts.
source: NO and PGE2 secretion by osteocytes in response to mechanical stimulation have anabolic effects on osteoblasts (Rochefort et al., 2010).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Rochefort et al., 2010.

claim: Receptor activation of nuclear factor-κ B ligand (RANKL), the osteoclast differentiation factor, is mainly produced by osteocytes.
source: Receptor activation of nuclear factor-κ B ligand (RANKL), the osteoclast differentiation factor, is mainly produced by osteocytes (Nakashima et al., 2011).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Nakashima et al., 2011.

claim: Osteocytes regulate neutrophil development through secretion of soluble factors like IL19.
source: Osteocytes regulate neutrophil development through secretion of soluble factors like IL19 (Xiao et al., 2021) and can also regulate myelopoiesis through Gsα-dependent and -independent pathways (Fulzele et al., 2013; Azab et al., 2020).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Xiao et al., 2021.

claim: Osteocytes can regulate myelopoiesis through Gsα-dependent and -independent pathways.
source: Osteocytes regulate neutrophil development through secretion of soluble factors like IL19 (Xiao et al., 2021) and can also regulate myelopoiesis through Gsα-dependent and -independent pathways (Fulzele et al., 2013; Azab et al., 2020).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to Fulzele et al., 2013 and Azab et al., 2020.

claim: Aging is associated with dysfunction of osteocytes.
source: In addition, studies have shown that aging is associated with dysfunction of osteocytes.
evidence: General statement about aging and osteocyte dysfunction.

claim: Degeneration of osteocytes lacuna-canalicular network had been observed in older adults and the aging animal model.
source: Degeneration of osteocytes lacuna-canalicular network had been observed in older adults (Busse et al., 2010) and the aging animal model (Tiede-Lewis et al., 2017).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to Busse et al., 2010 and Tiede-Lewis et al., 2017.

claim: Senescent osteocytes and their senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) have been shown to contribute to age-related bone loss.
source: Senescent osteocytes and their senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) have been shown to contribute to age-related bone loss (Farr et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2020).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to Farr et al., 2016 and Kim et al., 2020.

claim: DMP1 is a protein highly expressed in late-stage osteocytes but has been shown not to be essential for early skeletal development.
source: The latter is a protein highly expressed in late-stage osteocytes but has been shown not to be essential for early skeletal development (Feng et al., 2003).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Feng et al., 2003.

claim: Sarcopenia usually occurs concurrently with osteoporosis during aging.
source: Sarcopenia usually occurs concurrently with osteoporosis during aging (Clynes et al., 2021).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Clynes et al., 2021.

claim: Osteocyte-specific ablation of Cx43 impaired muscle formation.
source: Consistent with our observation, previous studies have reported that osteocyte-specific ablation of Cx43 impaired muscle formation (Shen et al., 2015).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Shen et al., 2015.

claim: Osteocyte-derived factors have been shown to stimulate myogenic differentiation in vitro.
source: Osteocyte-derived factors have also been shown to stimulate myogenic differentiation in vitro (Huang et al., 2017).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Huang et al., 2017.

claim: Specific deletion of Mbtps1 in osteocyte promotes soleus muscle regeneration and increase its size with age.
source: On the contrary, specific deletion of Mbtps1 in osteocyte promotes soleus muscle regeneration and increase its size with age (Gorski et al., 2016).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Gorski et al., 2016.

claim: Sclerostin, an osteocyte-derived circulating protein, is negatively correlated with skeletal muscle mass.
source: Sclerostin, an osteocyte-derived circulating protein, is negatively correlated with skeletal muscle mass (Kim et al., 2019).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Kim et al., 2019.

claim: A previous study showed weak Dmp1 expression in skeletal muscle fibers.
source: Previously there has been a study showing weak Dmp1 expression in skeletal muscle fibers (Lim et al., 2017).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Lim et al., 2017.

claim: Senescent osteoprogenitors have reduced self-renewal capacity and predominantly differentiate into adipocytes as opposed to osteoblasts.
source: Senescent osteoprogenitors have reduced self-renewal capacity and predominantly differentiate into adipocytes as opposed to osteoblasts (Chen et al., 2016; Li et al., 2017; Rosen et al., 2009).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to Chen et al., 2016; Li et al., 2017; Rosen et al., 2009.

claim: Fat-induction factors inhibit osteogenesis during adipogenesis.
source: Also, fat-induction factors inhibit osteogenesis during adipogenesis (Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Chen et al., 2016.

claim: Besides the production of RANKL from osteogenic cells like osteocytes and osteoblasts, other cells like adipocyte and T cell, also secret RANKL to regulate bone metabolism.
source: As for enhanced osteoclastogenesis, besides the production of RANKL from osteogenic cells like osteocytes and osteoblasts (Nakashima et al., 2011; Fumoto et al., 2014), other cells like adipocyte and T cell, also secret RANKL to regulate bone metabolism (Yu et al., 2021; Hu et al., 2021; Djaafar et al., 2010; Takayanagi et al., 2000).
evidence: Statement supported by multiple citations.

claim: B cell can produce OPG to regulate RANKL/OPG axis.
source: Also, B cell can produce OPG to regulate RANKL/OPG axis (Li et al., 2007).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Li et al., 2007.

claim: Progenitor cells can receive a long-lasting impact from the in vivo local microenvironment, where these cells are situated.
source: In support of this, previous studies have suggested that progenitor cells can receive a long-lasting impact from the in vivo local microenvironment, where these cells are situated. Isolation of cells for in vitro cell differentiation or even transferring cells to healthy mice would not alter their original in vivo phenotypes (Cao et al., 2020; Isaac et al., 2014; Ding et al., 2022; Edgar et al., 2021; Li et al., 2022).
evidence: Statement supported by multiple citations.

claim: Osteocyte regulates myelopoiesis via Gsα-dependent and -independent signaling.
source: Previous studies have reported that osteocyte regulates myelopoiesis via Gsα-dependent and -independent signaling (Fulzele et al., 2013; Azab et al., 2020).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to Fulzele et al., 2013 and Azab et al., 2020.

claim: Osteocyte mTORC1 signaling regulates granulopoiesis via secreted IL-19.
source: A recent study also reported that osteocyte mTORC1 signaling regulates granulopoiesis via secreted IL-19 (Xiao et al., 2021).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Xiao et al., 2021.

claim: Sclerostin secreted by osteocyte adversely affects B cell survival.
source: Meanwhile, sclerostin secreted by osteocyte adversely affects B cell survival (Horowitz and Fretz, 2012).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Horowitz and Fretz, 2012.

claim: Osteoblastic cell supports megakaryopoiesis and platelet formation.
source: Interestingly, a previous study has shown that osteoblastic cell supports megakaryopoiesis and platelet formation (Xiao et al., 2017).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Xiao et al., 2017.

claim: Osteocyte ablation induces lymphoid organ atrophy, thymocyte depletion, and altered fat metabolism in 'osteocyte-less' mice model.
source: Nevertheless, a previous study showed that osteocyte ablation induces lymphoid organ atrophy, thymocyte depletion, and altered fat metabolism in 'osteocyte-less' mice model (Sato et al., 2013), suggesting the role of osteocytes in the extraskeletal system.
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Sato et al., 2013.

claim: The skeletal system contains a series of sophisticated cellular lineages arising from the mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) that determine the homeostasis of bone and bone marrow.
source: The skeletal system contains a series of sophisticated cellular lineages arising from the mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) and hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) that determine the homeostasis of bone and bone marrow.
evidence: General statement about skeletal system composition.

claim: The skeletal system hosts at least more than 12 types of cell lineages arising from hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs).
source: The skeletal system hosts at least more than 12 types of cell lineages arising from hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) and mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) (Méndez-Ferrer et al., 2010).
evidence: Statement supported by citation to Méndez-Ferrer et al., 2010.

claim: During hematopoiesis, HSCs give rise to lymphoid and myeloid lineage cells, including B cells, neutrophils, monocytes, as well as osteoclasts.
source: During hematopoiesis, HSCs give rise to lymphoid and myeloid lineage cells, including B cells, neutrophils, monocytes, as well as osteoclasts.
evidence: General statement about hematopoiesis.

claim: MSCs differentiate into osteoblastic lineage cells, bone marrow adipocytes, and form fibroconnective tissues.
source: Meanwhile, MSCs differentiate into osteoblastic lineage cells, bone marrow adipocytes, and form fibroconnective tissues.
evidence: General statement about MSC differentiation.

claim: During aging, cell lineage commitments change rigorously and cause imbalance between myeloid–lymphoid hematopoiesis and adipo-osteogenic differentiation.
source: During aging, these cell lineage commitments change rigorously and cause imbalance between myeloid–lymphoid hematopoiesis and adipo-osteogenic differentiation (Chen et al., 2016; Sinha et al., 2022), which lead to the increased myelopoiesis and adipogenesis as opposed to lymphopoiesis and osteogenesis.
evidence: Statement supported by citations to Chen et al., 2016 and Sinha et al., 2022.

claim: Aging leads to increased myelopoiesis and adipogenesis as opposed to lymphopoiesis and osteogenesis.
source: During aging, these cell lineage commitments change rigorously and cause imbalance between myeloid–lymphoid hematopoiesis and adipo-osteogenic differentiation (Chen et al., 2016; Sinha et al., 2022), which lead to the increased myelopoiesis and adipogenesis as opposed to lymphopoiesis and osteogenesis.
evidence: Statement supported by citations to Chen et al., 2016 and Sinha et al., 2022.

claim: Cellular senescence is characterized by cell proliferation arrest, altered metabolism, and apoptosis resistance.
source: It has been speculated that cellular senescence, characterized by cell proliferation arrest, altered metabolism, and apoptosis resistance (Gorgoulis et al., 2019; Tchkonia et al., 2013), may be responsible for the regulation of lineage cell fates.
evidence: Statement supported by citations to Gorgoulis et al., 2019 and Tchkonia et al., 2013.

claim: The sarcopenia and muscle atrophy phenotype is most likely caused by the disturbance of osteocyte-muscle crosstalk.
source: However, our histology finding of no obvious changes in the total number of nuclei of muscle in partial ablation of DMP1-positive osteocytes suggested that the sarcopenia and muscle atrophy phenotype is most likely caused by the disturbance of osteocyte-muscle crosstalk.
evidence: Inference based on the observation that muscle fiber numbers were not reduced despite sarcopenia.

claim: Severe kyphosis observed in these osteocyte ablation mice supports the hypothesis of direct osteocyte-muscle crosstalk as kyphosis is the direct result of the significant bone loss and sarcopenia.
source: Certainly, further studies based on a more specific osteocyte ablation model are needed to understand the link of osteocytes between osteoporosis and sarcopenia. Nevertheless, severe kyphosis observed in these osteocyte ablation mice supports our hypothesis of direct osteocyte-muscle crosstalk as kyphosis is the direct result of the significant bone loss and sarcopenia (Wijshake et al., 2012; Woods et al., 2020).
evidence: Statement supported by citations to Wijshake et al., 2012 and Woods et al., 2020.

claim: Induction of SASP in both osteoprogenitors and myeloid progenitors may account for the impaired osteogenesis and induced osteoclastogenesis.
source: We speculated that induction of SASP in both osteoprogenitors and myeloid progenitors may account for the underlying cause.
evidence: Speculation based on the observed SASP accumulation and phenotypic changes.

claim: Senescence accumulation in osteoprogenitors led to the impaired osteogenesis.
source: Thus, senescence accumulation in osteoprogenitors led to the impaired osteogenesis.
evidence: Inference based on the observed senescence and impaired osteogenesis.

claim: Osteoprogenitors and BMMs have been primed by the altered bone microenvironment in DTAhet mice before in vitro differentiation.
source: Our study has suggested that osteoprogenitors and BMMs have been primed by the altered bone microenvironment in DTAhet mice before in vitro differentiation.
evidence: Inference based on the observation that in vitro phenotypes persist even after removal from the in vivo environment.

claim: Osteocyte may also participate in regulating platelet formation.
source: In our study, the number of MEP (erythrocyte and platelet precursors) was also reduced, and scRNA-seq analysis showed no significant change in erythrocyte population (data not shown), inferring that osteocyte may also participate in regulating platelet formation.
evidence: Inference based on the reduction of MEP and no change in erythrocyte population.

claim: B cell development was impaired along the immature B to mature B cell transition in DTAhet mice.
source: In addition, while the proportion of common lymphoid progenitors (CLP) was not altered in DTAhet mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 2I and J), total B220+ lymphoid cells reduced remarkably after osteocyte ablation (Figure 5O and P), in which DTAhet mice showed a relatively lower proportion of early B cell (pro-B pre-B, immature B, and transitional B cell) and a relatively higher proportion of late B cell (early mature B and late mature B) (Figure 5Q and R), which suggested that B cell development was impaired along the immature B to mature B cell transition in DTAhet mice.
evidence: Inference based on the altered proportions of B cell developmental stages.

claim: Osteocyte ablation accelerated neutrophil maturation.
source: As scRNA-seq revealed that neutrophils underwent a significant change after osteocyte ablation, neutrophil population were further reclustered into four subclusters from G1 to G4 (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A and B) and G4 population was significantly increased in DTAhet mice compared to WT mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 3C and D), which implied that osteocyte ablation accelerated neutrophil maturation.
evidence: Inference based on the increased G4 population, which represents more mature neutrophils.

claim: Osteocyte ablation altered neutrophil functions.
source: Genes related to glycolysis and necroptosis were also upregulated (Figure 5—figure supplement 3G and H), indicating that osteocyte ablation altered neutrophil functions.
evidence: Inference based on the upregulation of genes related to glycolysis and necroptosis.

claim: Osteocytes ablation induced lymphoid–myeloid malfunction in the bone marrow.
source: Also, the number of B cells was significantly less in DTAhet mice than that in WT mice (Figure 5D and E), which implicated that osteocytes ablation induced lymphoid–myeloid malfunction in the bone marrow.
evidence: Inference based on the reduced B cells and expanded neutrophils.

claim: Osteocytes deletion altered HSPC differentiation.
source: The result showed that DTAhet mice had stronger directionality of velocity vectors from the HSPC population to the neutrophil population compared to WT mice (Figure 5F), implying that osteocytes deletion altered HSPC differentiation.
evidence: Inference based on RNA velocity analysis showing stronger directionality toward neutrophil differentiation.

claim: HSCs in DTAhet mice bone marrow were mobilized.
source: Although there was no significant change in HSC (Lin-c-Kit+Sca1+, LSK+ cell) numbers between DTAhet and WT mice (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A and B), DTAhet mice demonstrated significantly increased number of short-term HSCs (ST-HSCs) with decreased number of long-term HSCs (LT-HSCs), indicating that HSCs in DTAhet mice bone marrow were mobilized (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C and D).
evidence: Inference based on the shift from LT-HSCs to ST-HSCs.

claim: Osteocyte ablation altered hematopoietic lineage, characterized by the shift from lymphopoiesis to myelopoiesis.
source: Together, these results demonstrated that osteocyte ablation altered hematopoietic lineage, characterized by the shift from lymphopoiesis to myelopoiesis.
evidence: Summary statement based on the collective findings on hematopoietic changes.

claim: Cell senescence of osteoprogenitors and myeloid lineage cells was associated with ablation of osteocyte.
source: Together, these results suggested that cell senescence of osteoprogenitors and myeloid lineage cells was associated with ablation of osteocyte.
evidence: Summary statement based on the senescence findings.

claim: Senescence in osteoprogenitors and myeloid lineage cells led to the impaired osteogenesis and increased osteoclastogenesis, respectively.
source: Together, our data suggested that senescence in osteoprogenitors and myeloid lineage cells led to the impaired osteogenesis and increased osteoclastogenesis, respectively.
evidence: Summary statement based on the senescence and differentiation findings.

claim: Osteocytes ablation impaired osteogenesis and promoted osteoclastogenesis.
source: Together, osteocytes ablation impaired osteogenesis and promoted osteoclastogenesis.
evidence: Summary statement based on the osteogenesis and osteoclastogenesis findings.

claim: DTAhet mice had systemic muscle atrophy and sarcopenia.
source: Together, these results suggested that DTAhet mice had systemic muscle atrophy and sarcopenia.
evidence: Summary statement based on the muscle findings.

claim: Sarcopenia was caused by the impairment of osteocyte-muscle crosstalk.
source: It is most likely that sarcopenia was caused by the impairment of osteocyte-muscle crosstalk.
evidence: Inference based on the observation that muscle fiber numbers were not reduced despite sarcopenia.

claim: Osteocyte ablation led to the accelerated skeletal aging.
source: Together, these data demonstrated that osteocytes ablation caused severe osteoporosis and kyphosis, as well as sarcopenia, which occurred at the very early stage compared to normal aging process. These age-related skeletal phenotypes combined with shortened lifespan demonstrated that osteocyte ablation led to the accelerated skeletal aging.
evidence: Summary statement based on the collective findings of osteoporosis, kyphosis, sarcopenia, and shortened lifespan.

claim: DTAhet mice displayed increased adipogenesis and decreased osteogenesis.
source: Together, these results suggested that DTAhet mice displayed increased adipogenesis and decreased osteogenesis.
evidence: Summary statement based on the bone marrow fat accumulation and reduced osteoblast findings.

claim: Increased adipogenesis, T cell expansion, and decreased B cell number may compensate for the altered RANKL/OPG axis.
source: In our model, increased adipogenesis, T cell expansion (data not shown), and decreased B cell number may compensate for the altered RANKL/OPG axis.
evidence: Speculation based on the observed changes in cell populations and RANKL/OPG ratio.

claim: Chondrogenesis was not altered after osteocyte ablation.
source: In addition, the mRNA levels of cartilage anabolism-related genes (Col1a2, Acan, Sox9, and Prg4) and catabolism-related genes (Mmp3, Mmp13, Adamts1, and Adamts5) were not significantly changed (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D), indicating that chondrogenesis was not altered after osteocyte ablation.
evidence: RT-qPCR analysis showing no significant changes in chondrogenesis-related genes.

claim: Increased adipogenesis and alteration of MSC commitment occurred after osteocyte ablation.
source: Meanwhile, the mRNA level of adipogenic markers, including Adipoq, Fabp4, Pparg, and Cebpa, was significantly increased (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C), indicating increased adipogenesis and alteration of MSC commitment after osteocyte ablation.
evidence: RT-qPCR analysis showing increased adipogenic marker expression.

claim: Diphtheria toxin (DT) had an accumulative effect with age in DTAhet mice.
source: About 80% empty lacunae was observed in DTAhet mice at 13 weeks, which increased by about 20% compared to 4 weeks (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C), indicating that diphtheria toxin (DT) had an accumulative effect with age in DTAhet mice.
evidence: Quantification data showing increased empty lacunae over time.

claim: The impairment of osteocyte network occurred in DTAhet mice.
source: Further, reduced dendrites were also observed in residual osteocytes of DTAhet mice (Figure 1C and D), indicating the impairment of osteocyte network.
evidence: Observation of reduced dendrites suggests impaired osteocyte network.

claim: Although there was partial ablation of osteocyteDMP1 in DTAhet mice, the embryonic development of skeletal tissue appeared to be normal.
source: Together, these results indicated that although there was partial ablation of osteocyteDMP1 in DTAhet mice, the embryonic development of skeletal tissue appeared to be normal.
evidence: Summary statement based on the whole-mount skeleton staining showing no apparent differences at E19.0.

claim: The progressive bone loss was observed through the life of DTAhet mice.
source: The progressive bone loss was observed through the life of DTAhet mice.
evidence: Summary statement based on the μCT findings at different time points.

claim: There was a giant increase of thoracic and lumbar curvature of DTAhet mice.
source: Whole-body μCT scan revealed that there was a giant increase of thoracic and lumbar curvature of DTAhet mice (Figure 2M).
evidence: Whole-body μCT scan shown in Figure 2M.

claim: No muscle fibrosis was observed in DTAhet mice at 4 weeks.
source: No muscle fibrosis was observed.
evidence: Histological observation of muscle tissue at 4 weeks.
